notes.definition: Alkenes are hydrocarbons with a carbon to carbon double bond (C=C). They form a homologous series with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ, and they are unsaturated because they contain two fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms.
explanation: Alkenes are hydrocarbons, so they contain only hydrogen and carbon atoms. What makes them different from alkanes is that every alkene molecule contains one carbon to carbon double bond, C=C. This double bond is the functional group of the alkenes: it is the part of the molecule that decides how alkenes react. Because of the double bond, the two carbon atoms involved each have one fewer bond available for hydrogen.

The alkenes form a homologous series. A homologous series is a family of compounds that have the same general formula and the same functional group, so they have similar chemical reactions. Each member differs from the next by a CH₂ unit, and physical properties such as boiling point change gradually along the series. The general formula of the alkenes is CₙH₂ₙ, so the number of hydrogen atoms is always twice the number of carbon atoms.

The first four members of the alkene homologous series are ethene (C₂H₄), propene (C₃H₆), butene (C₄H₈) and pentene (C₅H₁₀). There is no alkene with only one carbon atom, because a double bond needs two carbon atoms. You only need to know the names of these four alkenes, but you should be able to recognise any alkene from its formula. The name ending '-ene' shows a C=C double bond, while '-ane' shows an alkane.

Alkenes are described as unsaturated. An alkane such as ethane, C₂H₆, holds the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms, so it is saturated. Ethene, C₂H₄, has two fewer hydrogen atoms than ethane, because two of the carbon bonds are used in the double bond. This means more atoms can be added across the double bond, which is why alkenes are much more reactive than alkanes and decolourise bromine water.

Alkenes can be represented by a molecular formula, for example C₃H₆, or by a displayed formula that shows every atom and bond, with the double bond drawn as two lines. When you draw a displayed formula, check that every carbon atom has four bonds in total (a double bond counts as two) and every hydrogen atom has one.
keyFacts: Alkenes are hydrocarbons with a C=C double bond.
The C=C double bond is the functional group of the alkenes.
General formula of the alkenes: CₙH₂ₙ.
First four alkenes: ethene C₂H₄, propene C₃H₆, butene C₄H₈, pentene C₅H₁₀.
Alkenes are unsaturated: they have two fewer H atoms than the alkane with the same number of C atoms.
Alkenes form a homologous series: same general formula, same functional group, similar reactions.
In a displayed formula each C has 4 bonds; the double bond counts as 2.
The smallest alkene is ethene; there is no one-carbon alkene.

keyTerms.definition: A hydrocarbon containing a carbon to carbon double bond, with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ.
Containing a carbon to carbon double bond, so other atoms can be added to the molecule.
Containing only single carbon to carbon bonds.
The atom or group of atoms that determines how a molecule reacts; for alkenes it is C=C.
A family of compounds with the same general formula and functional group, which have similar chemical properties and differ by CH₂.
A formula that applies to every member of a homologous series, such as CₙH₂ₙ for alkenes.
Two shared pairs of electrons between two atoms, shown as two lines in a displayed formula.

equations.name: General formula of the alkenes
equations.formula: number of H atoms = 2 × number of C atoms

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think 'unsaturated' means the alkene can dissolve more of something.
misconceptions.right: In fact unsaturated means the molecule contains a C=C double bond and fewer hydrogen atoms than the corresponding alkane.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often draw the carbon atoms in a C=C bond with three hydrogens each, like an alkane.
misconceptions.right: In fact each carbon in the double bond has only two other bonds left, so in ethene each carbon has just two H atoms.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think methene (CH₂) is the first alkene.
misconceptions.right: In fact a double bond needs two carbon atoms, so ethene, C₂H₄, is the first alkene.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think any hydrocarbon with an even number of H atoms is an alkene.
misconceptions.right: In fact the number of H atoms must be exactly twice the number of C atoms (CₙH₂ₙ); alkanes also have even numbers of H atoms.

realWorld: Ethene is made in huge quantities by steam cracking and used to make poly(ethene), the most common plastic.
Ethene gas is released by ripening fruit; it is used in warehouses to ripen bananas evenly.
Propene is the monomer for poly(propene), used in food containers, ropes and carpets.
separateOnlyContent: All of this subtopic is for separate Chemistry (8462) only: the general formula CₙH₂ₙ, the names ethene, propene, butene and pentene, and the meaning of unsaturated. Combined Science students only need to know that alkenes are produced by cracking and decolourise bromine water.
examTips: Learn both general formulae and use them to classify: alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ.
When drawing alkenes, draw the double bond as two clear parallel lines and count four bonds on every carbon.
Define unsaturated precisely: contains a C=C double bond (two fewer H than the alkane).
The specification lists ethene, propene, butene and pentene; you do not need names for other alkenes.
summary: Alkenes contain a C=C double bond, their functional group.
They have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ.
The first four are ethene, propene, butene and pentene.
Alkenes are unsaturated: two fewer H atoms than the matching alkane.
They form a homologous series with similar reactions.
They can be shown by molecular or displayed formulae.

questions.question: What is the general formula of the alkenes?
questions.explanation: Alkenes have twice as many H as C atoms. CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ is the alkane formula and CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH is the alcohol formula.

questions.question: Which bond is found in every alkene molecule?
questions.explanation: The carbon to carbon double bond is the functional group of the alkenes.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of propene.
What is the molecular formula of propene?
questions.explanation: Propene has 3 carbon atoms, so 2 × 3 = 6 H atoms. C₃H₈ is propane, the alkane.

questions.question: Which compound is an alkene?
questions.explanation: C₄H₈ fits CₙH₂ₙ (butene). The others fit CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so they are alkanes.

questions.question: Why are alkenes described as unsaturated?
options: They contain a carbon to carbon double bond
They do not dissolve in water
markScheme: 1 mark: they contain a C=C double bond
questions.explanation: The double bond means they have two fewer hydrogen atoms than the corresponding alkane, and more atoms can be added.

questions.question:
An alkene has the formula C₅H₁₀.
What is the name of this alkene?
questions.explanation: Pent = 5 carbon atoms; C₅H₁₀ fits CₙH₂ₙ, so it is an alkene: pentene. Pentane is C₅H₁₂.

questions.question:
An alkene and an alkane have the same number of carbon atoms.
How many hydrogen atoms does the alkene have compared with the alkane?
questions.explanation: Compare CₙH₂ₙ with CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: the alkene has 2 fewer H atoms, e.g. ethene C₂H₄ and ethane C₂H₆.

questions.question: Which statement about the members of a homologous series is not correct?
options: They have the same general formula
They have the same functional group
Each member differs from the next by CH₂
markScheme: 1 mark: they have identical boiling points
questions.explanation: Physical properties such as boiling point show a gradual trend along a series; they are not identical. Chemical reactions are similar because the functional group is the same.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of propene.
How many C–H bonds are shown in Figure 1?
questions.explanation: Propene, C₃H₆, has 6 hydrogen atoms and each forms one bond to carbon, so 6 C–H bonds (plus one C=C and one C–C).

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the formulae of the first four alkenes.
An alkene has 7 carbon atoms in each molecule.
How many hydrogen atoms does one molecule of this alkene contain?
questions.explanation: CₙH₂ₙ with n = 7 gives 2 × 7 = 14 (C₇H₁₄).

questions.question:
Propene has the formula C₃H₆.
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of propene.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1
questions.explanation: Carbon contributes 36 and hydrogen 6, giving 42.

questions.question:
Butene has the formula C₄H₈.
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of butene.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1
questions.explanation: Carbon contributes 48 and hydrogen 8, giving 56.

questions.question:
An alkene has a relative formula mass (Mr) of 112.
Calculate the number of carbon atoms in one molecule of the alkene.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1
questions.explanation: The alkene is C₈H₁₆: 96 + 16 = 112.

questions.question:
Pentane has the formula C₅H₁₂ and pentene has the formula C₅H₁₀.
Calculate the difference between the relative formula masses (Mr) of pentane and pentene.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): C = 12   H = 1
questions.explanation: The only difference is two hydrogen atoms (2 × 1 = 2), so the Mr values differ by 2.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formula of an alkene with the formula C₂H₄.
Name the alkene shown in Figure 1.
questions.explanation: Eth = 2 carbon atoms, -ene = alkene. Do not confuse with ethane, C₂H₆.

questions.question: Give the functional group present in all alkenes.
markScheme: 1 mark: C=C (carbon to carbon double bond)
questions.explanation: The C=C bond gives alkenes their characteristic reactions.

questions.question: Describe the displayed formula of ethene, C₂H₄.
acceptedAnswers: two carbon atoms joined by a double bond
each carbon bonded to two hydrogen atoms
markScheme: 1 mark: two C atoms joined by a double bond (C=C)
1 mark: each C atom bonded to two H atoms by single bonds
questions.explanation: Each carbon has four bonds: two in the double bond and one to each of two hydrogen atoms.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formulae of ethane and ethene.
Explain why ethene is unsaturated but ethane is saturated.

markScheme: 1 mark: ethene has a C=C double bond / two fewer H atoms
1 mark: ethane has only single C–C bonds
questions.explanation: Saturated means only single carbon to carbon bonds; unsaturated means there is a C=C double bond.

questions.question: Give two features of a homologous series.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any two: same general formula; same functional group; similar chemical reactions; each member differs by CH₂; gradual change in physical properties
questions.explanation: The alkenes are a homologous series: CₙH₂ₙ, C=C functional group, each differing by CH₂.

questions.question:
An alkene has 9 carbon atoms in each molecule.
Give the molecular formula of this alkene.
State whether the alkene is saturated or unsaturated.
questions.explanation: 2 × 9 = 18 hydrogen atoms. All alkenes are unsaturated because of the C=C bond.

questions.question: Explain why there is no alkene with only one carbon atom.
acceptedAnswers: double bond needs two carbon atoms
markScheme: 1 mark: the functional group is a carbon to carbon double bond
1 mark: so at least two carbon atoms are needed
questions.explanation: The C=C bond joins two carbon atoms, so the smallest alkene is ethene.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formulae of ethane and ethene.
Use ideas about bonding to explain why an alkene has two fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms.

acceptedAnswers: one less bond for hydrogen on each of two carbons
markScheme: 1 mark: each carbon atom forms four bonds
1 mark: the double bond uses two bonds on each of the two carbon atoms
1 mark: so each of these carbon atoms can bond to one fewer hydrogen atom, two fewer in total
questions.explanation: In ethane each carbon has 3 H; in ethene each has 2 H, because the extra C–C bond replaces one C–H bond on each carbon.

questions.question:
A hydrocarbon has the formula C₆H₁₀.
Is the hydrocarbon an alkane, an alkene or neither?
Explain your answer.
markScheme: 1 mark: an alkane would be C₆H₁₄ and an alkene C₆H₁₂
questions.explanation: C₆H₁₀ fits neither general formula, so it is a different type of hydrocarbon.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the displayed formulae of propane and propene.
Compare the structures of propane and propene.
In your answer, refer to bonding, general formulae and the meaning of saturated and unsaturated.
markScheme: Indicative content: both are hydrocarbons with three carbon atoms; propane is an alkane with only single C–C bonds; propene is an alkene with one C=C double bond; propane fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, propene fits CₙH₂ₙ; propene has two fewer H atoms; propane is saturated, propene is unsaturated; each carbon forms four bonds in both.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear comparison of bonding and formulae, correct use of saturated and unsaturated.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two correct differences.
questions.explanation: A comparison needs points about both molecules, e.g. 'propane has only single bonds, whereas propene has a C=C double bond'.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the formulae of four hydrocarbons, A, B, C and D.
Classify each hydrocarbon as an alkane or an alkene, and name the compounds where you can.
Explain how the structure of the alkenes differs from the structure of the alkanes.
Explain why the alkenes form a homologous series.
markScheme: Indicative content: A C₂H₄ fits CₙH₂ₙ, alkene, ethene; B C₄H₁₀ fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkane, butane; C C₅H₁₀ alkene, pentene; D C₆H₁₄ alkane (hexane, name not required); alkenes contain a C=C double bond, alkanes only single bonds; alkenes are unsaturated, alkanes saturated; alkenes have two fewer H atoms; alkenes share the general formula CₙH₂ₙ and the functional group C=C; ethene and pentene differ by three CH₂ units; similar chemical reactions; gradual trend in physical properties.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): all four classified correctly with reasons from the general formulae, named where possible, clear structural difference and a full description of a homologous series.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): most classified correctly with some explanation of structure or homologous series.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two classified with little explanation.
questions.explanation: Use the general formulae to classify, then explain the structural difference (C=C) and the homologous series features.

questions.question:
Butene has the formula C₄H₈.
Which statement describes the displayed formula of butene?
options: Four carbon atoms with only single bonds
Four carbon atoms with one C=C double bond
Four carbon atoms with two C=C double bonds
Four carbon atoms and an O–H group
markScheme: 1 mark: four C atoms with one C=C double bond
questions.explanation: Butene is an alkene, so it has one C=C bond. Only single bonds would be butane, C₄H₁₀.

questions.question: Give the name of the alkene that has 4 carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: But = 4 carbon atoms, -ene = alkene. Its formula is C₄H₈.
